### Dex SDK 1.38.0

- Every package requires Dex SDK 1.38.0 (`dex-python-sdk==1.38.0`, `@superdurable/dex` `1.38.0`, Go `sdk-go` `v1.38.0`) and a Dex Server with protocol 4: server-zd v0.1.17 or later, as with 1.35.0.
- Agents CI, the nightly long run, and the publish workflows test against `dexcli` 1.38.0.

### The session graph for Dex Web

- Python and TypeScript cores: `render_session_flow_graph` (`renderSessionFlowGraph`) and the `dex-agents-session-graph` command render the Flow Definition Graph 2.0 file of an agent's session Flow, with the application's Flow type and Action permission. Dex Web loads it with `--flow-rendering-dir`, draws the session Steps, and offers `resolve_interrupt`, `answer_question`, `steer_user_message`, and `cancel_turn` as Actions without a condition. Both cores write the same bytes.
- The graph is derived from the Python core's registered Flow and source and ships in both packages. The conformance suite adds `session_graph.json`, and each core's tests fail when the graph and the session Flow disagree.
- Dex Web needs a release that accepts Actions without a condition and calls no RPC for a view without fields.
- Go core: no graph. It registers only part of the session Flow.
- See [Show sessions in Dex Web](https://github.com/superdurable/dex/blob/agents/v0.3.0/docs/content/agent-frameworks/deploy-agents.mdx).

### Compaction in framework adapters

- The OpenAI Agents SDK (Python and TypeScript), Pydantic AI, LangChain and LangGraph, Google ADK, Vercel AI SDK, and Mastra adapters implement the compaction methods, so `AgentSessionOptions.compaction` works with them. A session compacts with the existing `CompactContext` Step and stores a `ContextSummary`, so retention can delete messages behind it. Without a policy nothing changes, and a session started on 0.2.0 starts compacting once its Workers have one.
- Adapters compact only between turns, before a turn's first model call. A model call that resumes a turn after its tool calls never compacts, because the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph resume from a run state that holds the input.
- The adapters' session flow functions take `compaction`, `retained_message_limit`, and `summary_model` (`summaryModel`). LangGraph needs `summary_model`, because a compiled graph does not expose its model. The TypeScript OpenAI Agents and Mastra session flow functions now forward `compaction` and the message storage options to the core.
- Google ADK: the summary ends with a line that carries the ADK session state and the agent that replied last, so the rebuilt session keeps both.
- Claude Agent SDK: unchanged. Claude Code compacts its own transcript, and the adapter takes no compaction policy.
- Python and TypeScript cores: new helpers for adapters, `estimate_text_tokens`, `estimate_stored_input_tokens`, `select_turn_boundary_cutoff`, `describe_stored_message`, and `build_context_summary_prompt` (camelCase in TypeScript). The Stepwise summary texts move to the core's root module and stay exported from Stepwise.
- `CompactionPolicy.reserved_input_tokens` (`reservedInputTokens`), default 0, adds tokens the runner's estimate cannot see.
- `dex_agents.testing` and `@superdurable/dex-agents/testing` add `ContextWindowModelScript` and `ContextWindowSessionScenario`.
- No stored value changes. The conformance suite adds the summary prompt texts.
- Go core: unchanged.
- See [Compaction and the storage bound](https://github.com/superdurable/dex/blob/agents/v0.3.0/docs/content/agent-frameworks/deploy-agents.mdx#compaction).

### Spend limits

- Python and TypeScript cores: the new `ModelSpendLimit` interface is an application's spend limit. Pass it as `AgentSessionOptions.spend_limit` (`spendLimit`), or on a Stepwise `AgentDefinition`. The session calls `check_model_call` before each attempt of `RunModel` and `CompactContext`, and `report_model_usage` when the attempt's model call returns. Without one, nothing changes. Counters and limits belong to the application.
- A refused call ends the turn. `AgentState.last_turn_error` starts with the new `MODEL_CALL_REFUSED_ERROR_PREFIX` (`modelCallRefusedErrorPrefix`), then the reason. The session keeps running and checks again on the next message.
- A check that raises or takes longer than `SPEND_LIMIT_CALL_TIMEOUT`, 30 seconds, fails closed: it fails the attempt, and the Step retries. A report that raises is logged and dropped. `ModelUsageReport.report_id` is stable per attempt.
- Python Claude Agent SDK adapter: `claude_agent_session_flow` takes `spend_limit`. A harness is checked once per turn segment, and its usage arrives when the segment ends.
- No stored value changes. The conformance suite adds the refusal prefix.
- Go core: unchanged. It does not check spend limits.
- See [Spend limits](https://github.com/superdurable/dex/blob/agents/v0.3.0/docs/content/agent-frameworks/deploy-agents.mdx).

### A configurable RunModel limit

- Python and TypeScript cores: `AgentSessionOptions.run_model_limit` (`runModelLimit`) sets the method timeout and attempts of `RunModel`, with the new `RunModelLimit`. The retry budget moves with them: the method timeout times one less than the attempts, and at least twice the method timeout. The default stays 15 minutes and 3 attempts in 30 minutes. `CompactContext` and the heartbeat timeout do not change.
- Python Claude Agent SDK adapter: `claude_agent_session_flow` takes `run_model_limit`. The TypeScript adapter takes it through its session options. A turn segment that needs more than 15 minutes can now finish. A failed segment reruns whole.
- No stored value changes. A running session gets the limit on its next `RunModel` after the Worker restarts.
- Go core: unchanged.

### Sessions are searchable by the Step they wait in

- Python core: `AgentSessionClient.start_session` sets `FlowConfig.active_step_search_mode` to the new `AGENT_SESSION_ACTIVE_STEP_SEARCH_MODE` (`WITH_WAIT_FOR`), so `ActiveStepTypes = "AwaitToolApproval"` and `"AwaitQuestionAnswer"` find a session while it waits and drop it when it moves on. A mode set in `options.config_override` wins, including `DISABLED`.
- TypeScript core: the new `startAgentSession(client, flow, sessionId, input, options)` does the same, with the new `agentSessionActiveStepSearchMode`. Until this core supports a Dex SDK with `ActiveStepSearchMode.WITH_WAIT_FOR`, the value is `ActiveStepSearchMode.DEFAULT`, which the server treats the same way. `AgentSessionTestClient.startSession` calls it.
- `Client.startFlow` and `AsyncClient.start_flow` are unchanged, so a session they start stays out of this search. So do sessions started on 0.2.0, until `UpdateFlowConfig` turns it on. No stored value changes.
- Go core: unchanged.
- See [Find sessions that need a person](https://github.com/superdurable/dex/blob/agents/v0.3.0/docs/content/agent-frameworks/deploy-agents.mdx).

### A session at the state limit fails, with the reason

- Python and TypeScript cores: when a Step fails on `limits.maxFlowStateBytes`, the session ends. `RecordTurnFailure`, `RecordToolFailure`, and `RecordToolOutcomeUnknown` recognize the recovery error (`ValueTooLarge` with the text `run state of <X> bytes exceeds the maximum of <Y> bytes`, or `active run state of ...` from a server that counts only active state), set the new `AgentState.status` value `failed` with that text in `last_turn_error`, and close the Flow `FAILED` with the same text in the same commit. A session no longer goes on to pay for model calls whose answers cannot be stored. A value over `values.maxValueBytes` still fails only its turn.
- That commit is checked against the same limit, and it can fail too. The Flow then closes `FAILED` with the text anyway and `AgentState` keeps its last value, which is also what happens for a Step with no failure route, such as `AwaitUserMessage`. `AgentSessionClient.get_agent_snapshot` and the new `read_agent_snapshot` (`readAgentSnapshot`) read the Flow's close, so they report `failed` and the reason for any session that stored a state, for one more call to Dex. A session that fails before it stores a state keeps a snapshot with no state. The `get_agent_snapshot` RPC alone reads only what was stored.
- UI streams: the event SSE generators end once the Flow failed and every event was sent, instead of sending keep-alives forever. A TypeScript UI message stream that finds the Flow failed ends with an `error` part with the reason and `finishReason` `error`. `AgentSessionUIMessages` has a new `failure` field.
- New messages are refused. `AgentSessionClient.send_user_message` and `steer_user_message`, and the new `sendAgentUserMessage`, raise the new `AgentSessionFailedError`, a `FlowNotActiveOrNotFoundError` with `reason`. A direct RPC call still gets `FlowNotActiveOrNotFoundError`.
- Queued messages never run. They stay readable in `AgentSnapshot.queued_messages` until retention deletes the session.
- Go core: reads `failed` and keeps its behavior. It does not end a session at the limit yet.
- See [Upgrade agent code while sessions wait](https://github.com/superdurable/dex/blob/agents/v0.3.0/docs/content/agent-frameworks/deploy-agents.mdx) for the order of a rolling deploy.
